city.Nauru.description: This tiny island in the central Pacific is one of the smallest countries on Earth — you can drive all the way around it in under half an hour. Years of digging up phosphate rock left its middle a rocky moonscape.
city.Nauru.landmark: jagged coral-limestone pinnacles of the island's interior with the blue Pacific beyond
city.Nauru.greeting: In Nauruan, a warm welcome is “Ekamowir omo.”
city.Nauru.flag: doodled a blue flag with one thin yellow stripe across the middle and a single white star below it
city.Nauru.clue.0: wondered about a tiny speck of an island floating all alone in the central Pacific
city.Nauru.clue.1: was tickled that you could drive the whole way around it in under half an hour
city.Nauru.clue.2: was curious about an island whose middle was dug up into strange rocky pinnacles
city.Nauru.clue.3: wanted to visit one of the very smallest island countries in the whole world
city.New Zealand.description: These two large islands in the South Pacific are known for green mountains and misty fiords, bubbling geysers and mud pools, far more sheep than people, and the Māori haka — a powerful ceremonial dance.
city.New Zealand.landmark: Mitre Peak rising steeply from the dark waters of Milford Sound with waterfalls and mist
city.New Zealand.greeting: In Māori, hello is “Kia ora” (KEE-ah OR-ah).
city.New Zealand.flag: blue with a Union Jack and four red stars of the Southern Cross
city.New Zealand.clue.0: booked a ticket toward a pair of green islands way down in the South Pacific
city.New Zealand.clue.1: kept giggling about a land that has far more sheep than people
city.Samoa.description: This group of islands in the South Pacific sits at the heart of Polynesia. It is famous for hand-tapped tattoos, welcoming villages led by chiefs, and the deep, round To Sua swimming hole reached by a tall ladder.
city.Samoa.flag: pinned on a flag badge: bright red with a small blue corner holding five white stars
city.Samoa.clue.0: studied a map of a cluster of islands sitting at the very heart of Polynesia
city.Samoa.clue.1: planned to watch tattoos being tapped into skin by hand with tools used for hundreds of years
city.Solomon Islands.description: This chain of nearly a thousand tropical islands in the South Pacific is known for its warm lagoons, coral reefs, sunken World War II ships that divers love to explore, and a fiery underwater volcano nicknamed the Sharkcano.
city.Solomon Islands.landmark: maze of jungle islands and turquoise water of the Marovo Lagoon seen from above
city.Solomon Islands.greeting: Many people speak Pijin — say hello with “Halo” (HAH-loh).
city.Solomon Islands.flag: blue and green split by a yellow diagonal stripe, five white stars in the corner
city.Solomon Islands.clue.0: dreamed of peering at a hidden underwater volcano nicknamed the Sharkcano
city.Solomon Islands.clue.1: packed scuba gear to dive over sunken warships from a big war long ago
city.Tonga.description: This kingdom of scattered islands in the South Pacific is the only Pacific nation never colonized, and it still has its own king. It is known for friendly villages, ancient stone monuments, and warm seas where humpback whales come to visit.
city.Tonga.landmark: humpback whale and her calf swimming in clear blue water
city.Tonga.greeting: In Tongan, hello is “Mālō e lelei” (MAH-loh eh leh-LAY).
city.Tonga.flag: mostly red with a white corner holding a red cross
